---
title: "check-div-ids.yml"
---

Diff-scoped, warn-only check that flags a fenced div
with a theorem-type class but no id with the matching prefix.
Quarto and the lab's `callouty-theorem` and `custom-callout` extensions
build a callout, a number and a cross-reference target from the id,
so a div written `::: {.remark}` renders as a plain block quote
([lds#1600](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/lds/pull/1600)).

| Class | Needs an id starting |
| --- | --- |
| `.definition` | `#def-` |
| `.theorem` | `#thm-` |
| `.lemma` | `#lem-` |
| `.corollary` | `#cor-` |
| `.proposition` | `#prp-` |
| `.remark` | `#rem-` |
| `.example` | `#exm-` |
| `.exercise` | `#exr-` |

The check reports a div when the pull request adds its opening line.
It does not look inside code fences, HTML comments or blockquotes,
and it reports nothing for a div that was already in the file.
Other classes on the div, such as `.notes`, are fine.

With no base ref, or when the diff cannot be computed,
the check skips with a warning instead of scanning the whole tree.
Set `whole-tree: true` to measure a corpus.

## Inputs

- `globs`: git pathspecs of files to check (default `*.qmd`).
- `paths-ignore`: glob patterns to skip.
- `fail`: block instead of warn (default false).
- `whole-tree`: scan every matching file, not only a pull request's additions.

## Example

[`examples/check-div-ids.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-div-ids.yml)
